title: SEER — Sustainable Electricity Expansion Roadmaps
summary: Democratizing power systems planning for a robust and sustainable energy transition.
overview: Power system planning shapes investments in generation and grid infrastructure. Fragmented data and inaccessible tools can limit participation in these decisions, particularly in the Global South. SEER aims to make planning faster, more flexible, and more accessible to energy-sector stakeholders.

The project is developing an open dataset to support machine learning approaches, including automated input-data generation and models that approximate optimization solvers. Collaboration with planning practitioners is central to making the tools useful for real decisions.

title: Multi-Stakeholder Perspectives of Electric Bus Service in Kigali, Rwanda
summary: Understanding passenger satisfaction and perceptions of electric bus services in Kigali.
overview: The project examines multiple stakeholder perspectives on electric bus services in Kigali, Rwanda.

In August 2024, Miquilina Anagbah led data collection with University of Rwanda students. Surveys with about 800 electric and diesel bus passengers examined service satisfaction and perceptions of electric buses.

title: Energy Transition Demand Modeling Study for Rwanda
summary: Studying household energy use and opportunities for electricity demand growth in Rwanda.
overview: The study examines energy-transition demand in Rwanda in collaboration with KCRC, Rwanda Energy Group, and the eGUIDE initiative.

From May to August 2025, Eliane Nirere participated in fieldwork surveying more than 2,000 low-income households in Kigali. About 370 participating households received efficient electric kettles through a cost-sharing scheme, with electricity and appliance use to be monitored over six months.
